plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, MUU, SPAL) to zero for capital preservation.
Trim QQQI to 20% to reduce concentration and meet mandate.

conservative.read: This conservative plan targets a modest ~1.5% per month, prioritizing capital preservation. Expect lower volatility and drawdowns, but also limited upside potential. The focus is on stability and avoiding significant losses.

plan: Trim SOXL to 3%, MUU to 2%, and SPAL to 1% to reduce overall leverage.
Trim QQQI to 25% to meet the single-name concentration mandate.
Sell SMH and QQQ due to their downtrends and scanner flags.
Buy XLV at 5% to add diversification with a strong scanner setup.
This plan balances risk and growth, maintaining a moderate cash buffer.
balanced.read: This balanced plan aims for ~2.5% per month, focusing on risk-first growth. It seeks a blend of broad index, quality tech, and limited leverage. Expect moderate volatility and drawdowns, with reasonable growth potential.

plan: Trim QQQI to 25% to meet the single-name concentration mandate.
Sell SMH and QQQ due to their downtrends and scanner flags.
Add to SOXL and MUU to 6% each, and SPAL to 3%, increasing leveraged exposure.
Buy XLV at 6% to add a high-scoring scanner setup.
This plan leans into leverage and concentration for aggressive growth.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets ~4% per month, aiming for stretched growth. It utilizes leveraged ETFs and concentrates in high-scoring setups. Be aware of significantly higher volatility, potential for larger drawdowns, and the daily decay/rebalancing of leveraged ETFs.

plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, MUU, SPAL) to zero to reduce risk.
Add to QQQI to 30% to increase income-generating exposure.
Sell SMH and QQQ due to their downtrends and scanner flags.
Add to SPY to 30% for broad market exposure and stability.
This plan prioritizes steady monthly distributions and low drawdown.
income.read: This income plan targets ~1% per month, focusing on parking cash for yield. It prioritizes low drawdown and reliable income over growth. Remember that distributions are variable and NAV can still fall in a selloff; this is not a savings account.
